_about: Sentinel research library — one row per distinct method found in the Telegram channel 'MQL5 Algo Trading' (@mql5dev, the official MetaQuotes channel). Every row cites the post ids it was built from (t.me/mql5dev/<id>); the loader (research_library.py) attaches each post's date and the mql5.com article or CodeBase item it links to. 'author' is the mql5.com author only where the post names one — the channel's posts are MetaQuotes summaries of community articles and rarely name authors, so most rows say so. 'evidence' records what the posts themselves show; screenshots, win rates and returns are claims. 'interpretation' marks what is mine rather than the author's. Nothing in this file has been executed; code attachments were never run. Photos: the channel's post images were reviewed from the owner's Telegram Desktop export for the key cited posts (tg_media_notes in research.db); where an image carries numbers they are quoted in 'evidence' as what the image shows — still the author's claim.

rows.title: Session-window entry filter (trade only in the instrument's main liquidity session)
rows.author: not named in the posts (mql5.com community articles; #3292 is a five-year study by its article author)
rows.claim: Restricting entries to the instrument's main session improves expectancy more than regime or trend filters. #3292: raw MACD(12,26,9) histogram crossovers on US_TECH100 H1 gave +0.017R/trade over 2,213 trades (PF 1.03); a 14:00-20:00 broker-time window gave 195 trades at +0.100R (PF 1.20); ADX/ATR-percentile regime and EMA200 filters 'added little'.
rows.evidence: #3292 states backtest numbers in R on one instrument, one feed (AvaTrade), five years, pessimistic same-bar fills. Others: logic only.
rows.limitations: One instrument and one signal type in the only quantified post; the window was chosen on the same data; broker time, not UTC; no placebo comparison; the other posts assert sessions without numbers.

rules.instruments: US_TECH100 in #3292; London/NY for FX and gold in the others
rules.entry: unchanged base signal, taken only if the signal bar closes inside the window
rules.filters: 14:00-20:00 broker time (#3292); London 07:00-16:00 / New York 12:00-21:00 elsewhere
rules.exits: unchanged (#3292: TP 3.0 ATR, SL 2.5 ATR, 48-bar timeout)

missing_rules: treatment of trades open at the window's end
rows.interpretation: Mine: the mechanism is probably two-fold — narrower spreads (lower cost_r) and better follow-through in the cash session — so the test must separate cost from signal (run at fixed cost and at measured session cost). Sentinel has only the 02:00-06:00 UTC dead zone today.
rows.relation_to_sentinel: complement: a new gate on the ARIA signal; cheapest candidate to test on the existing replay

rows.title: ADX trend-strength gate (ADX above a threshold and rising, DI direction agreeing)
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Trend-pullback and breakout entries do better when ADX(14) is above 20-25 and rising; #4301 exits when ADX < 18; #4196 (Seykota-style) uses ADX > 20 to avoid ranges; #3418 reads ADX < 25 as weak, 25-50 workable, > 50 climactic.
rows.evidence: Logic only in every post except #3292, which found an ADX-based regime filter 'added little' after the session filter, and #3544, which reports an Optuna-tuned ADXR gate without numbers in the post.
rows.limitations: Thresholds differ by post (18/20/23/25); ADX lags; #3292 is the only quantified test and is negative for the regime layer.

rules.entry: base signal only when ADX >= threshold (20-25) and ADX rising vs the prior bar; +DI/-DI must agree with direction

rows.interpretation: Mine: ARIA already requires EMA stacking and structure, which overlaps with what ADX measures; the gate may remove few trades. Test as a gate and as a component-removal (ADX instead of the 4h trend).
rows.relation_to_sentinel: complement/overlap with the EMA-stack and 4h-trend gates

rows.title: Persistence / randomness regime gates: Hurst exponent, lag-1 autocorrelation, fractal dimension, approximate entropy, Shannon entropy
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Trend and breakout signals only pay when returns show persistence: Hurst > 0.55 (rolling R/S, lookback ~200), lag-1 autocorrelation above its +Z/sqrt(N) band, FDI < 1.5, ApEn below an upper threshold; near-random regimes turn signals into cost. #2413 tested an autocorrelation threshold on SMA-crossover trades over 16 years of M15 EURUSD/GBPUSD (numbers not in the post).
rows.evidence: Logic only, plus a reference to literature for Hurst; #2413 claims a backtest without numbers.
rows.limitations: Window lengths, thresholds and smoothing vary; Hurst on 200 bars is noisy; the measures are correlated with each other and with ADX; no post shows a placebo-controlled gain.

rules.entry: base signal only when the chosen measure indicates persistence
rules.indicators: Hurst (R/S, lookback 200, EMA 5), lag-1 autocorrelation (window N, bands +/-Z/sqrt(N)), FDI (boundary 1.5), ApEn (m=2, r=0.2 SD, window 50-200)
rules.filters: H > 0.55 trend / < 0.45 reversion; FDI < 1.5; ApEn below threshold

missing_rules: what to do in the neutral band
rows.interpretation: Mine: one family, not five; test one representative (lag-1 autocorrelation over 100 bars, the cheapest and best-understood) and only then others.
rows.relation_to_sentinel: complement; bounded parameters; high risk of fitting

rows.title: H4 swing-structure context gate (HH/HL vs LH/LL labels decide which lower-timeframe setups are allowed)
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Reading market structure from H4 swing points (HH, HL, LH, LL) and allowing lower-timeframe patterns only when the H4 state agrees avoids misclassified reversals inside ranges and stops intraday noise from flipping the trend read.
rows.evidence: Logic only.
rows.limitations: Swing strength window is a free parameter; swing labels confirm late; no numbers.

rules.timeframes: H4 structure, entries on lower TFs
rules.entry: lower-timeframe setup only when the H4 label sequence matches the pattern's prerequisite
rules.indicators: H4 swing points with a configurable strength window
rules.conditions: H4 read regardless of trading timeframe

missing_rules: how many labels define a state
rows.interpretation: Mine: Sentinel's 4h EMA20/50 trend is a smoother version of the same idea; a swing-label version may react faster to turns and lag less at 4h boundaries. Candidate component swap, not an addition.

rows.title: Spread gate relative to the stop or to ATR (skip entries when the cost is a large share of the risk)
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Skip an entry when the live spread exceeds a share of the stop distance (10 % in #4282), an ATR-normalised threshold (#2850), or its own recent percentile (#3730); cost spikes at rollover and news are the trades to avoid.
rows.evidence: Logic only; #4282 includes the rule in a backtested EA but does not isolate its effect.
rows.limitations: Needs a live spread (Sentinel has estimates plus optional measured samples); percentile versions need a warm-up; the rule interacts with the session filter (spreads widen outside sessions).

rules.entry: base signal only when spread / stop distance <= cap (0.10) or spread <= k x ATR
rules.filters: cap 10 % of stop (#4282); GREEN/YELLOW/RED percentile states (#3730)

rows.interpretation: Mine: in Sentinel's accounting this is a cap on cost_r at entry; it is a legitimate rule (do not pay a fifth of the stop to enter) but partly tautological in replay, since cost_r is subtracted anyway. The honest test uses measured spreads by hour, not the flat estimate.
rows.relation_to_sentinel: complement; interacts with L01 and L34

rows.title: Economic-calendar blackout around high-impact releases
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Pausing new entries N minutes before and after high-impact events for the symbol's currencies avoids spread spikes and whipsaws; #3246 warns the Strategy Tester has no calendar history, so such filters never fire in backtests unless a CSV event list is supplied.
rows.evidence: Logic only.
rows.limitations: No post quantifies the gain; historical calendars must be sourced; Sentinel's live NAS100 news-week block is manual and replay has it off.

rules.entry: blocked inside the window
rules.filters: impact high; pre/post buffers 15-60 min; NFP/FOMC extended

rows.interpretation: Mine: not testable on the one-year Deriv history without a historical calendar; park until an event feed exists, then test with #3246's CSV approach.

rows.title: Multi-timeframe agreement filters (higher-timeframe candle colour, EMA order on several timeframes, all-timeframe oscillator agreement)
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Take lower-timeframe signals only in the direction of the higher timeframe (D1 candle colour for M5 in #552; D1 RSI for H1 in #3051; three-horizon MA agreement in #3824; all tracked timeframes must agree in #2974). #2126 notes dual-timeframe crossovers often fail to carry from backtest to forward test.
rows.evidence: Logic only; #2126 shows backtest screenshots and admits forward degradation.
rows.limitations: Many variants, no isolated effect sizes; higher-timeframe reads lag at boundaries (the same 4h-boundary issue Sentinel has).

rules.timeframes: pairs such as M5/D1, H1/D1, H4/D1/W1
rules.entry: base signal only when the higher timeframe agrees
rules.indicators: candle colour, EMA order, RSI, Williams %R, MA direction

rows.interpretation: Mine: Sentinel's 4h EMA trend already is this filter. The useful test is whether a D1 layer on top of 4h adds anything, and whether the 4h layer itself earns its place (component removal).

rows.title: Volatility-regime gating (ATR percentile bands, GARCH variance forecast, range index)
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Trade only in a chosen volatility regime: #3847 signals only in the LOW percentile regime; #4172 gates on GARCH(1,1) expansion; #4083/#3806 skip range-breakout days when the range vs daily ATR is extreme; #3228 argues ATR lags shocks and GARCH forecasts (alpha 0.09, beta 0.90) should size stops.
rows.evidence: Logic only; #3292 reports its ATR-percentile regime layer added little.
rows.limitations: Contradictory directions (low vs expanding volatility) across posts; ARIA already has an ATR band gate (0.6-1.8 x its 100-bar mean).

rules.entry: base signal only inside the chosen regime
rules.indicators: ATR percentile over 100-250 bars, GARCH(1,1), Gopalakrishnan Range Index

rows.interpretation: Mine: ARIA's ATR-band gate passes > 76 % of signals; a stricter band is a one-parameter ablation of an existing gate rather than a new idea.

rows.title: ATR-multiple trailing stop that never loosens (volatility stop, Chande-Kroll, chandelier)
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Trail the stop at k x ATR (commonly 2.0-3.0) behind the best price, ratcheting only in the trade's favour; #2420 claims a double-EMA trail beat calibrated fixed SL/TP and SAR trails; #4283 scores an ATR trail against a 10-bar channel and a fixed 2R target.
rows.evidence: #2420 and #4283 state backtest numbers (screenshot-level); the rest is logic.
rows.limitations: k and ATR period are free parameters; #4283's winning exit is named 'B' without definition in the post; results vary by year and instrument.

rules.entry: unchanged
rules.exits: stop = best price -/+ k x ATR, ratchet only; optional breakeven after a threshold
rules.conditions: closed bars; one-way ratchet; tick-size quantisation (#4208)

missing_rules: whether ATR is frozen at entry or recomputed
rows.interpretation: Mine: Sentinel's 7.2c trails 1R behind best after +1R; the ATR version is the same idea with a volatility unit and no arming threshold. Cheapest to test as another shadow rule on the forward journal and in replay.
rows.relation_to_sentinel: overlap/alternative to the 7.2c trail; fits the shadow mechanism

rows.title: Exit lab: run several exits in parallel on the same entries and score them in R
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: On Turtle System-1 breakouts, three parallel exits (ATR trail, 10-bar channel, fixed 2R) scored in R on XAUUSD H4 showed one exit leading in 2025 (+66.20R) and 2026 (+22.35R), H1 leadership varying by year, and EURUSD/GBPUSD/USDJPY 2026 flat to negative.
rows.evidence: Backtest numbers in R in the post; non-repainting; stop assumed first when stop and target fall inside one bar (the same convention Sentinel uses).
rows.limitations: Exit 'B' undefined in the post; no costs mentioned; per-year leadership changes suggest noise.
rows.interpretation: Mine: Sentinel's shadow design is exactly this; the insight is to add the channel exit and the pure ATR trail as shadows and to report per-year leadership rather than one total.

rows.title: MAE/MFE-calibrated stops, targets and scale-out rungs
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Measure every trade's maximum adverse and favourable excursion in R; set the stop at the winners' p90 MAE, targets or partial-close rungs at percentiles of recent MFE (#4260 self-calibrates the ladder); low capture ratio means exits give back gains, MAE barely above the stop means the stop is noise.
rows.evidence: Logic only; the tools report measurements but no post shows the calibrated exits beating fixed ones out of sample.
rows.limitations: Calibrating on the same trades that are evaluated is in-sample by construction; needs a minimum-sample gate and a chronological split.

rules.entry: unchanged
rules.exits: rungs at MFE percentiles (e.g. p25/p50/p75) of the last N trades; partial close per rung

rows.interpretation: Mine: Sentinel already stores mfe_r/mae_r; the diagnostic half (where trades die) is free and goes into the review's diagnosis; the calibrated-exit half must be walk-forward only.

rows.title: Staged stop management: breakeven after a threshold, delayed trailing to avoid spread stop-outs, loss-only exits on adverse excursion or invalidation
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Move the stop to entry after +1R (or a point/ATR threshold), start trailing only after a profit cushion so spread noise does not stop the trade, and cut losers early on ATR adverse excursion, time-in-trade or EMA 20/50 invalidation (#4200).
rows.evidence: Logic only.
rows.limitations: Thresholds are free; early-cut rules can convert would-be winners into small losses; none quantified.

rules.entry: unchanged
rules.exits: breakeven at +1R; trail after cushion; loss-only exits at k x ATR adverse, T bars, EMA invalidation

rows.interpretation: Mine: 7.2c's arm-at-+1R trail is already a staged rule; the untested half is the loss side (time stop before 96 bars, invalidation exit). Sentinel's forward data shows 0 time-outs, so a time stop would rarely fire.

rows.title: Time-based exits (session end, Friday close, fixed holding time)
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Close at a fixed time (session end, Friday hour, next open) instead of waiting for a stop; intraday-only trading limits overnight reversals (#776, a trader's advice without data).
rows.evidence: Logic only; #4121's fixed hold is part of a quantified study (see L23).
rows.limitations: Interacts with every other exit; costs of forced exits at illiquid times.

rules.entry: unchanged
rules.exits: flat at session end / Friday HH:MM / after T bars

rows.interpretation: Mine: for 15m setups a session-end flat rule pairs naturally with L01; test only together with it.

rows.title: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck derived stop and target instead of grid-searched SL/TP
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Grid-searching SL/TP on Sharpe fits path noise; fitting a discrete OU process to per-trade P&L gives a risk-bounded stop and forecast-driven target that is more robust (#3306, 100,000 synthetic paths); OU bands can replace Bollinger/Keltner for entries when mean reversion (theta > 0) is detected (#3470).
rows.evidence: Reference to literature and synthetic-path simulation; no market backtest in the post.
rows.limitations: Assumes OU dynamics of trade P&L; not directly applicable to a trailing exit.
rows.interpretation: Mine: a caution against tuning SL/TP multipliers, which the lab must respect (plateaus, not peaks); not a candidate itself.

rows.title: Donchian / Turtle breakout systems (20- and 55-bar breakouts, N-based stops, pyramiding), including a gold H4 variant above EMA200
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: #4282: XAUUSD H4, long when the last closed bar closes above the prior 20-bar high and price is above the 200 EMA, stop 2 x ATR(20), fixed 2R target, skip when spread > 10 % of the stop: Jan 2020-Sep 2026 net +9,029.72 on a 10k deposit, PF 1.77, max DD 11.38 %, 198 trades, 46.97 % wins, returns concentrated in 2024-2025, shorts negative, 2020-2023 yearly -2.9 % to +5.1 %. #3760: original Turtle rules on EURUSD show low win rate and larger winners (numbers truncated). #4283: the same entry with three exits (see L10).
rows.evidence: Backtest numbers stated in the posts (#4282 the most complete); no walk-forward, no placebo; concentration in two years is stated by the author. Export photo for #4282 (reviewed 5 Oct): MT5 balance curve 'XAUUSD H4, 2020.01.01–2026.09.20, default inputs (buys only), 198 trades, net +9,029.72 on 10,000, PF 1.77, max equity DD 11.38 %, 1 % risk, random delay' — flat for roughly the first 115 trades, all of the gain in the last ~80.
rows.limitations: Gold's 2024-2025 trend makes any long-only breakout look good; shorts were negative; the 200 EMA and 2R target were chosen on the same data; MT5 tester spread assumptions unknown.

rules.entry: close of the last closed bar above the prior 20-bar high (long) / below the 20-bar low (short); #3760 adds a 55-bar system and a skip rule after a profitable breakout
rules.indicators: Donchian 20/55, EMA 200, ATR(20), N = Wilder TR(20)
rules.filters: price above EMA 200 (#4282); spread <= 10 % of stop; no entries near session close
rules.exits: fixed 2R (#4282); 10/20-bar counter-breakout (#3760); ATR trail or channel (#4283)
rules.sizing: 1 % risk per unit; #3760 pyramids up to 4 units every N/2
rules.conditions: one position; market order at the next open

rows.interpretation: Mine: a genuinely different entry from ARIA's pullback logic, cheap to implement, honest costs on H4 (spread is a small share of a 2 x ATR stop). The right test is long-and-short on all focus markets with the 4h/daily trend as the only filter, chronological splits, and a check that the result is not two years of gold.

rows.title: Simple bar-breakout for indices with upside bias (close of bar 1 above high of bar 2, long-only, NAS100 H4)
rows.author: not named in the post
rows.claim: A long-only EA buying at the new-bar open when Close(1) > High(2), stop at Low(1), RR-based target, suits indices with persistent upside bias; the post references a ~3.5-year NAS100 H4 backtest on M1 OHLC and says real-tick validation is still required.
rows.evidence: Backtest referenced; numbers not in the post. Export photo for #3453 (reviewed 5 Oct): MT5 tester report — 589 long-only trades, PF 1.10, expected payoff 0.88 per trade on 10,000, Sharpe 0.73, win 54.2 %, max equity DD 3.65 %, up to 7 consecutive losses: a weak edge on the author's own numbers.
rows.limitations: Long-only on a rising index is mostly beta; stop at Low(1) can be tiny (cost share explodes); 'upside bias' is a selection on hindsight.

rules.entry: buy at next open when Close(1) > High(2)

rows.interpretation: Mine: include only as a control against L15 on NAS100 (does a simpler rule do as well?), with a minimum stop of 1 x ATR to keep cost_r sane.

rows.title: Session-range and opening-range breakouts (Asian range into London, first-N-minute range, Larry Williams volatility breakout)
rows.author: not named in the posts; #1771 reviews Concretum Group papers; #2781/#2811/#2827/#2837 are Larry Williams rules
rows.claim: Mark the high/low of a defined window (Asian session, first N minutes after an open, or a fraction of yesterday's range added to today's open) and trade the breakout with stop at the opposite side or an ATR fraction, target equal to the range or an RR multiple; filters: range width vs daily ATR (#4083, #3806), MA trend, ADR. #3751 frames how to research it: a bare baseline first, then filters, judged by trade counts (300-700 optimisation, 50-100 forward).
rows.evidence: Logic only in nearly every post; #1599 and #3980 mention backtests without numbers in the post; #1771 cites academic ORB papers (2020-2025) without figures in the post.
rows.limitations: Many free choices (window, buffer, target); the Deriv feed's session hours differ from CME/NYSE; 15m bars make the first-minutes range coarse.

rules.instruments: gold, FX majors, US indices, Nikkei
rules.timeframes: M5-M15 execution; D1 range for Williams
rules.entry: stop order or close beyond the window's high/low (+ buffer)
rules.indicators: session clock, ATR/ADR, optional MA/MACD/Stochastic filters
rules.filters: skip days where range / daily ATR is outside a band
rules.exits: range-sized target, RR target, session-end flat, trailing
rules.stops: opposite side of the range or ATR fraction
rules.conditions: one trade per session; confirmation over several bars in some variants

rows.interpretation: Mine: a second alternative family; cheaper than ARIA to compute; test the bare #3751 baseline on XAU and NAS100 15m before any filter.

rows.title: Trend-pullback entries: EMA retest, ATR-normalised pullback depth, Fibonacci golden zone, FVG pullback
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: In a trend (price vs EMA, HTF bias), enter when price pulls back to the EMA (pierce and close back, #2948), to the 61.8-78.6 % retracement of the last confirmed swing (#4013), into a fair-value gap (#3154), or when ATR-normalised distance to the EMA falls below a ratio after exceeding it (#3513); score pullbacks by depth relative to the impulse (#3487).
rows.evidence: Logic only across the family.
rows.limitations: Overlaps heavily with ARIA's Fibonacci-zone and structure gates; zone definitions differ (45-66.8 % in ARIA vs 61.8-78.6 % here).

rules.entry: close back with the trend after touching the EMA / zone
rules.indicators: EMA 20/50, ZigZag(13) swings, Fib levels, FVG 3-bar gaps, ATR

rows.interpretation: Mine: the actionable test is an ablation of ARIA's own Fib gate (45-66.8 % touched within 5 bars) against the deeper 61.8-78.6 % zone and against no zone at all; replay already shows the Fib gate passes only 15 % of signals.
rows.relation_to_sentinel: overlap with the Fibonacci and structure gates

rows.title: Daily trend-following templates: Seykota dual-EMA + ADX, Weinstein stage analysis, Minervini trend template
rows.author: not named in the posts (methods attributed to Ed Seykota, Stan Weinstein, Mark Minervini)
rows.claim: Multi-week D1 systems: EMA 20/200 direction with ADX > 20, ATR(20) x 3-5 stops, ATR risk parity and a 10-20 % portfolio heat cap (#4196); 150-day SMA stage transitions with volume expansion and RSI(14) >= 50 (#3600); 50/150/200 SMA alignment, rising 200 SMA, RSI > 50, breakout of the 20-bar high on 1.5 x volume, exit below the 50 SMA (#3753, backtests show few D1 signals and long idle periods).
rows.evidence: #3753 reports backtest behaviour qualitatively; others logic/literature.
rows.limitations: Daily systems need years, not one; Deriv history is one year; tick volume on CFDs is a weak proxy for volume.

rules.entry: EMA cross / stage transition / 20-bar high breakout with volume
rules.indicators: EMA 20/200, SMA 50/150/200, ADX, ATR(20), RSI(14), 20-bar volume average
rules.exits: EMA reversal, ATR stop, close below 50 SMA

rows.interpretation: Mine: outside Sentinel's 15m-4h scope and not testable on one year with enough trades; record, do not queue.

rows.title: Moving-average crossover variants (open/close MA pair, close-beyond-fast-MA confirmation, state-machine retracement entry, score-gated crossovers)
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Crossovers improved by: using one MA on opens and one on closes of equal period to cut lag (#1378, EURUSD backtest claimed), requiring the bar to close beyond the fast MA (#3083), waiting for a momentum candle then a retracement bar before a stop order (#3989), or printing only when a 7-8 factor score (VWAP, RSI, MACD, ADX, volume, HTF bias) meets a minimum (#3122, #3205).
rows.evidence: Backtest screenshots claimed in #1378/#1780/#2651; others logic only.
rows.limitations: The score-gated versions are ARIA-like composites with no evidence that the score ranks outcomes; MA crossovers on their own are known to be cost-negative intraday.

rules.entry: cross confirmed by close / score / retracement

rows.interpretation: Mine: #3122/#3205/#3252 are the same design as ARIA 7.1's 10-gate score, and ARIA's replay shows the score does not separate good from bad trades — a negative finding that applies to this whole family. Not queued.
rows.relation_to_sentinel: overlap (same design); negative evidence from Sentinel's own replay

rows.title: Mean-reversion entries (Bollinger re-entry, z-score bands, RSI2, Value Charts / MR Swing, OU bands)
rows.author: not named in the posts (#3425 cites Abrams and Walker 2010; #1704 cites Larry Connors)
rows.claim: Fade extremes: re-entry inside Bollinger bands after a close outside (#2219, #3822), z-score of (price - SMA)/SD beyond +/-2.5 on closed bars (#3444), Connors RSI2 on S&P 30-minute (#1704, 'rigorously backtested' without numbers), MR Swing with a 200-day SMA hysteresis regime (#3425, literature results). #1784 warns one-minute OHLC tests of such rules mislead; #2399 found a double-Bollinger system small-profit vs loss over five years.
rows.evidence: Mostly logic; #2399 and #3425 state results qualitatively or by literature.
rows.limitations: Opposite thesis to a trend-pullback system; mean reversion on CFDs pays the spread twice as often; results sensitive to bar-resolution assumptions.

rules.entry: re-entry inside bands / z-score beyond threshold / RSI2 extreme
rules.indicators: Bollinger(20,2), SMA, SD, RSI(2), Value Charts

rows.interpretation: Mine: not a modification of Sentinel; a possible challenger for the 'flat' 4h regime that Sentinel currently refuses to trade (7.2c blocks when the 4h trend is flat). Lower priority than breakouts because of cost sensitivity.
rows.relation_to_sentinel: contradiction (different regime); possible complement in flat regimes

rows.title: Liquidity-sweep / market-structure entries (sweep and reclaim, BOS/CHoCH, order blocks, fair-value gaps, Judas swing)
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Enter after price sweeps a confirmed swing high/low and closes back inside (reclaim), in the direction of a higher-timeframe trend (#4270: XAUUSD M15 with the H1 50 EMA; M1/M5 'underperformed due to spread', H1 'too few trades'); variants add break-of-structure confirmation, order-block or FVG zones, and session kill-zones. #4270 reports a sizing bug (tick value 10x) that caused 78 % drawdown over 107 trades before the fix.
rows.evidence: #4270 states tester runs qualitatively; others logic only. Export photo for #4270 (reviewed 5 Oct): 'SMC Gold, XAUUSD M15, 2026.01.01–2026.09.20 (real ticks): 127 trades, net +861.85, PF 1.10, max equity DD 10.63 %, 1 % risk, random delay'; the curve ends well below its peak.
rows.limitations: Definitions of swings, sweeps and zones vary; 'confirmed' swings confirm late; small stops at M1-M5 make spread dominant (stated by #4270 itself).

rules.entry: sweep of a confirmed swing then a reversal close through the sweep candle body

rows.interpretation: Mine: ARIA's 'fake break' MCC veto is the mirror of this idea (it refuses what these systems trade). A sweep-reclaim challenger on XAU 15m with the 4h trend is a clean contrast test; costs on 15m will decide.
rows.relation_to_sentinel: partial contradiction (ARIA vetoes fake breaks) / alternative

rows.title: Calendar and time-of-day anomalies: gold CME-reopen drift, Turnaround Tuesday, weekday effects, weekend-gap reversals
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: #4121: buying gold at the CME daily reopen and holding a fixed time showed, over 11 years of hourly data, a cost-corrected +1.60 bps/trade (t = 3.42, PF 1.30, 10 of 11 years positive, ~200 trades/yr), down from +3.34 bps when the reopen cost was understated (real-tick reopen cost ~60 points vs 19 assumed). #3468: Turnaround Tuesday had no stable edge on EURUSD/XAUUSD/SP500 2016-2026 as a baseline; ATR filtering and management lifted XAUUSD to +38 % and SP500 to +40 % (11 % max DD). #3543/#2865: weekday continuation/reversal research EAs. #3501/#3978/#4001: weekend-gap and 'Oops' gap reversals as rules.
rows.evidence: #4121 is the most carefully stated result in the whole channel (t-statistic, cost correction, year-by-year consistency); #3468 states backtest percentages; the rest is logic. Export photo for #4121 (reviewed 5 Oct): result card — as charged +3.34 bps (t 7.40, win 59.3 %); at the tester-measured cost +1.60 bps (t 3.42, win 50.8 %); +3.3 %/yr on capital exposed, max DD 4.6 %, Sharpe 1.23, 10 of 11 years positive, ~200 trades/yr, ~130 USD/yr at 0.01 lots. Export photo for #3468: balance curve only, no instrument/period visible.
rows.limitations: #4121's edge is 1.6 bps — below Deriv's XAU spread at the reopen unless held for hours and sized small; Deriv's gold session hours differ from CME; #3468's lift came from management added after seeing the baseline.

rules.entry: buy at the reopen (#4121); Tuesday open against Monday's direction (#3468)
rules.filters: one trade per session; optional ATR filter

rows.interpretation: Mine: worth a measured look on Deriv's XAU 1h bars around 23:00-00:00 UTC, strictly as a time-of-day study, because the claim is small, specific and cost-aware. Not a Sentinel modification.

rows.title: Short-term OHLC pattern rules (Larry Williams swing pivots, smash day, hidden smash day, inside-bar continuation, outside bar, double top/bottom state machines)
rows.author: not named in the posts (Larry Williams rules; Livermore Market Key in #4124)
rows.claim: Deterministic bar-relationship rules: three-bar pivots confirmed after close with outside/inside-bar exclusions (#2769); smash-day setups where a bar closes beyond N prior extremes, entry on the next bar's break (#2885, #2965); inside-bar continuation with a stop order beyond the mother bar (#3497); double tops/bottoms with neckline breaks (#4230, #4098).
rows.evidence: Logic only; built as 'research EAs' for the tester, no results in the posts.
rows.limitations: Small stops relative to spread on 15m; pattern frequency low on H4; no numbers.

rules.entry: break of the pattern bar's extreme / confirmed close

rows.interpretation: Mine: ARIA's candle and pattern gates already encode similar shapes; a pure-pattern challenger without the other gates is a component-removal test of ARIA (does the candle gate alone carry the information?).

rows.title: Score-gated multi-condition signals with grades (the same design as ARIA's 10-gate score)
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Weighted checks (EMAs, RSI, MACD, ADX, VWAP, volume, HTF bias) summed into a score; print graded A+/A/B/C signals only above a minimum; some auto-calibrate weights from recent R results (#3252).
rows.evidence: Logic only; dashboards show rolling win rate but no post shows that higher grades earn more.
rows.limitations: No evidence that the score orders outcomes; auto-calibration from recent R is in-sample by construction.
rows.interpretation: Mine: Sentinel's replay answers this family: 8/10 -0.044R, 9/10 -0.057R, 10/10 -0.35R on 4,341 trades. Recorded as a negative finding; the useful successor question is which single gates carry information (ablation), not a higher threshold.

rows.title: Supertrend direction with ADX strength (H4 trend system; adaptive-ATR variants)
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Trade closed-bar Supertrend(ATR 10, factor 3) direction only when ADX(14) >= 23 and DI agrees; exit on ADX < 18 or a flip (#4301); #4113 audits flips against TradingView signals rather than profit; adaptive variants shrink the ATR multiplier on divergence or efficiency-ratio changes.
rows.evidence: Logic only.
rows.limitations: Supertrend is a trailing-stop system in disguise; whipsaw cost in ranges; no numbers.

rules.entry: Supertrend flip direction with ADX >= 23 and DI alignment, on the previous bar's values
rules.exits: ADX < 18, Supertrend reversal, opposite signal; no fixed TP

rows.interpretation: Mine: a compact H4 trend challenger with four parameters; the exit-on-ADX rule is the novel part. Lower priority than L15 because Supertrend flips cluster in ranges.

rows.title: Machine-learning meta-labelling of rule signals (random forest / XGBoost / LSTM / HMM gates), kept only if the rejected trades are worse
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Train a classifier on features at signal time to veto or size rule-based entries (RSI mean reversion on EURUSD H1 with a 27-feature random forest under strict walk-forward, #3387; FLAML/ONNX gate on EMA crossovers, #3831; HMM regime posterior >= 0.6 plus GRU veto on ADX/DI entries on EURUSD H4, #4079, which states the right acceptance test: keep the layer only if rejected trades have worse expectancy and risk, not merely fewer trades). Counter-evidence in the same channel: a LightGBM triple-barrier baseline on ~144k M15 XAUUSD bars stayed at AUC ~0.50 (#4027); out-of-sample accuracy above 60 % still lost after costs (#4209).
rows.evidence: Mixed: #3387 describes walk-forward without numbers in the post; #4027 and #4209 are negative results stated with numbers. Export photo for #2847 (reviewed 5 Oct): tester report — 30 trades, 3,000 deposit, net +1,328, PF 1.25, max equity DD 58.56 %: too few trades and a ruinous drawdown.
rows.limitations: High complexity, many degrees of freedom, needs thousands of signals per training window; Sentinel's A-grade slices produce ~2 trades/day.

rules.entry: base rule signal passed through a trained gate
rules.indicators: ADX/DI, RSI, ATR-normalised features, hour-of-day, HMM states
rules.conditions: purged walk-forward training; single-use test set

rows.interpretation: Mine: deferred. Sentinel's signal stream is too thin for a gate to be trained honestly, and the channel's own quantified attempts on gold were null. Revisit only if the base rule has an edge to protect.

rows.title: Portfolio heat and correlation caps on simultaneous exposure
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Block or shrink new entries when summed open risk exceeds a heat cap (10-20 % of equity) or when a Pearson-correlation matrix shows the new trade amplifies existing exposure (#2991, #4116).
rows.evidence: Logic only.
rows.limitations: Rolling correlations are unstable; none quantified.
rows.interpretation: Mine: belongs to the risk layer, which the research system does not optimise; recorded because Sentinel's statistics assume trade independence while XAU 15m and XAU 1h open on the same move — the fix is in the evaluation (block bootstrap by week, one-trade-per-market variants), not in the strategy.

rows.title: Position-sizing models: ATR risk parity, Kelly / Leverage Space with Monte Carlo drawdown, drawdown-scaled risk, loss-streak cooldowns
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Size by risk % divided by the ATR stop (#4196), derive a Kelly budget from win rate and payoff then scale by ATR (#3146), cut risk after consecutive losses and restore after wins (#3162), map remaining daily budget to size through a sigmoid (#4069); Monte Carlo shows risking above 1-2 % sharply raises blow-up probability (#2199).
rows.evidence: Logic and simulation; no live numbers.
rows.limitations: All assume a positive edge to size; irrelevant until one exists.
rows.interpretation: Mine: Joel's 1 %/2 %/3 %/three-loss framework already is a conservative version; nothing here is adopted. Kept as the reason the review reports R, not money.

rows.title: Daily / weekly loss caps and equity-governance state machines (prop-firm style)
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Halt trading at a daily, weekly or total loss limit; four-state governance (NORMAL/CAUTION/RESTRICTED/LOCKDOWN) with hysteresis (#3452); simulate prop-firm rules in the tester with rolling restarts to expose start-date sensitivity (#3563).
rows.evidence: Logic only.
rows.limitations: Already present in the EA.
rows.interpretation: Mine: #3563's rolling-restart idea is useful for the review (report the worst 30-day window, not only max DD).
rows.relation_to_sentinel: already implemented in the EA; evaluation idea kept

rows.title: Placebo and permutation tests for filters and entries; sequential non-overlapping evaluation
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: A filter is only shown to work if the accepted subset beats random subsets of the same size drawn from all base entries (#3977, permutation placebo with a corrected p-value); any entry signal should be tested with sequential non-overlapping trades, a t-statistic, monthly consistency and a random-entry control (#3979), since overlapping windows inflate significance by about the square root of the horizon; price-bar permutation tests expose tester tricks (#74, #134); random-entry EAs lose exactly the spread (#3229, #2836, #2860).
rows.evidence: Methodological; #3229 shows the random baseline with numbers. Export photo for #3979 (reviewed 5 Oct): 'Gross edge never reaches the cost line' — XAUUSD, 40,802 signals May 2023–Aug 2026, average favourable move per 0.01 lot by holding period +0.043 (15 min), +0.208 (60), +0.062 (240), −0.533 (480) against a 0.31 USD transaction cost.
rows.limitations: Permutation tests need enough base trades; placebo draws must respect the one-position-per-slice constraint to be fair.
rows.interpretation: Mine: adopted as the acceptance test for every filter hypothesis in the lab (L01, L02, L03, L05): accepted-subset expectancy vs 1,000 placebo subsets of equal count, p < 0.05 after Bonferroni over the hypotheses tried.

rows.title: Overfitting controls: CSCV / probability of backtest overfitting, CPCV with purging and embargo, walk-forward efficiency, parameter plateaus
rows.author: not named in the posts (Bailey et al. CSCV; López de Prado CPCV; Masters' 1-SE rule)
rows.claim: Estimate the probability that the best in-sample configuration underperforms out of sample (CSCV/PBO); purge and embargo overlapping labels; measure walk-forward efficiency as OOS/IS Sharpe per window with 50 % as a pass; prefer parameter plateaus to peaks; short rolling Sharpe (40-60 bars) cannot separate skill from noise (#3521, Lo's SE).
rows.evidence: Methodological, literature-based.
rows.limitations: CSCV needs many configurations; Sentinel's candidates have few parameters, so plateau checks and walk-forward are the practical versions.
rows.interpretation: Mine: adopted: every parameterised candidate reports a neighbourhood table (plateau), a 3-month-fit / 1-month-test walk-forward, and the count of configurations tried for the multiple-comparison correction.

rows.title: Distributional checks on a trade list: bootstrap intervals, Monte-Carlo reordering for drawdown, profit concentration, Wilson lower bound, per-setup attribution
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Resample trade P&L (1,000 paths) to report median and 95th-percentile drawdown and ruin probability; test whether removing the best winner or best day destroys the result; score win rate by its Wilson lower bound against the breakeven rate; attribute P/L per setup id since one side can carry all the drawdown (#4244).
rows.evidence: Methodological.
rows.limitations: Bootstrap assumes exchangeable trades; dependence between overlapping trades needs block resampling.
rows.interpretation: Mine: adopted into the review metrics: block bootstrap by week, best-winner-removed expectancy, drawdown 95th percentile, Wilson lower bound on win rate, per-slice and per-direction attribution.

rows.title: Measuring real trading costs: live spread percentiles, per-second sampling, spread as a share of ATR, round-trip cost with swap and commission, breakeven cost cushion, swap drag on index CFDs, reopen costs, slippage and latency
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Bar spread fields understate the spread actually paid (XAUUSD: 20 points across 60 live readings vs an M1 field median of 6, #4114); tick-averaged spread underweights quiet minutes and hides rollover spreads (#4277); index CFD longs bleed -4.7 % to -9.9 %/yr in swap and swap consumed 44 % of one test's gross profit (#4147); gold's reopen cost was 60 points in real ticks vs 19 assumed (#4121); re-pricing a deal list finds the breakeven cost per trade and a cost cushion grade (#3638/#3709); random entries lose the spread (#3229).
rows.evidence: Several posts state measured numbers; the tools are read-only measurement utilities. Export photo for #4114 (reviewed 5 Oct): XAUUSD 0.01 lot measured on the account — live spread 20.0 pts vs M1 bar field 6.0 pts (3.3×); real round trip 0.200 USD vs 0.060 charged by a bar-field backtest; swap per night long −0.5842 USD, short +0.4098 USD, triple charge Wednesday. Mine: on gold a two-night long hold costs about three spreads — material for Sentinel's XAU 1h/4h longs, which are not charged swap today.
rows.limitations: Broker-specific; Deriv MT5 costs must be measured on Joel's own accounts (the existing /api/sentinel/costs sampling is the hook).
rows.interpretation: Mine: the single most important finding for Sentinel's numbers: a -0.046R system is inside the cost uncertainty. The research system must (a) report expectancy at estimated, x1.5 and x2 costs, (b) record cost provenance per trade, (c) report the breakeven cost per trade in R, and (d) model swap for 1h/4h holds once the MT5 spec is sampled.
rows.relation_to_sentinel: evaluation rule, adopted; blocked inputs: commission, swap, slippage samples

rows.title: Data-quality audits: tick coverage, contested OHLC bars, missing bars across feeds, broker data differences, look-ahead leakage from centred windows
rows.author: not named in the posts
rows.claim: Synthetic ticks make tight-stop systems look profitable (#4102); when a bar touches both stop and target, M1 OHLC resolution is wrong 23.84 % of the time for 20-point brackets on XAUUSD and 0 % for 500-point ones (#4123); the same breakout strategy differed by 2,300-4,400 net pips across three feeds (#3692); centred rolling windows leak future bars into features and inflate walk-forward results (#3832, #3908).
rows.evidence: Numbers stated in #4123 and #3692; the rest methodological. Export photo for #4123 (reviewed 5 Oct): wrong-way share by stop distance on XAUUSD, 27,844 bracketed trades over 30 days vs real ticks — 20 pts 23.84 % (62.6 % contested), 50 pts 8.25 %, 100 pts 1.66 %, 200 pts 0.18 %, 500 and 1,000 pts 0 %. Sentinel's gold stops (1.5 × 15m ATR, typically above 1,000 points) sit where the error is nil.
rows.limitations: Deriv's public feed is one source; its 15m bars from the WebSocket are the same bars the app charts, so replay/live parity on data is good, but MT5 (Deriv's broker feed) may differ from the WebSocket feed.
rows.interpretation: Mine: adopted: the integrity check counts feed gaps per cohort; the stop-first convention on contested bars stays and is reported (#4123 says the error is small for stops of 1.5 x ATR); a parity test between the WebSocket candles and MT5 candles is a blocked input until the bridge samples them.
